title: Tenant listing index on the tables where no index reaches all of one tenant's rows (one per table)
description:
Outcome: Export, deletion and usage need to list every row of one tenant without reading the whole table. Where PPY-cd5926 shows no dense index whose (prefixed) partition covers every row, add one sparse index "tenantId" sorted by id. Expected from today's schema (to be confirmed by the inventory): Automation, ReviewRequest, ReviewReadMark, ReviewRecipientRule, EditorialPolicy, EditorialCheckSettings, ReaderHandle, ReaderVote, ReaderFlag, plus any model whose indexes are all sparse. Reference does not need one (corpusId is required on every row), so it does not compete with PR #1239's publicFeedKey for Reference's next index. Each table gets exactly one new index, so all of them may ship in ONE release (the limit is per table), but never in the same release as another index on the same table. Dedicated sites step through it with the upgrade planner (PPY-d2cab9).

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): amplify/data/schema.ts and the function/plugin schema files for the listed models, amplify/data/resource.ts, scripts/test-schema-parity.ts, docs/tenant-key-inventory.md.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-listing-index.feature):
Scenario: Exporting a tenant reads no other tenant's rows
    Given 50 tenants with ReaderVote rows
    When "alpha" is exported
    Then ReaderVote is read through the tenantId index and the read count equals alpha's rows

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-cd5926, PPY-94d609, PPY-8f2c4f. Blocks PPY-e882ee. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: Schema parity; the GSI ledger check; request meter in the export test.
Rollout: One release adds one index on each listed table; backfill of tenantId must run before the index is relied on (a sparse index of an unbackfilled table is incomplete). On dedicated sites it ships with their adoption.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: two index changes land on one table in one deploy and CloudFormation fails. Mitigation: the GSI ledger check (PPY-8f2c4f) fails the PR.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: ADDS one GSI (tenantId + id) on each listed table, about 9 tables; one per table; may share a release across tables.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
